newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures seen testing 21,300 barrier.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures seen testing 21,300 barrier.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished firmer on improved sentiment and bullish technical signals on Wednesday, and dealers said the market could soon breach a stubborn barrier at 21,300 points.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract gained 265 points to end at 21,225 on moderate turnover of 17,700 lots.
A trader with a Japanese institution said stop-loss buy orders were triggered around 21,220, taking the December Nikkei to a high of 21,270, but it was unable to sustain the rally.
"If the Dow holds on to its highs tonight and the dollar/yen doesn't collapse, the market could go above 21,300," said the trader, adding that the next target would be 21,520.
He said dips below the 21,200 would provide good buying opportunities, with more solid support seen at 20,950.

Late afternoon comments by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita at a regular news conference that the economic recovery appeared to be becoming solid would underpin the Nikkei on Thursday, the dealer said.
"That's good news for the stock market because everybody wants to see the economy recover," he said.

A broker with a European futures house said the Nikkei also received a boost from a sharp drop in Japanese government bond markets, which fell on comments by senior officials who said the recent rise in bond prices was not in line with the economy's performance.
"There was talk of switching from bonds to equities. The market is massively overweight on bonds," he said.
